referenceFindings.title: Corrupt config.json is silently replaced with an empty configuration
referenceFindings.claim: loadChatConfig catches all read/parse errors and returns an empty config, so a transient/corrupt config.json can make all accounts/channels appear deleted without a visible recovery path or backup warning.

evidence.quote: try { ... JSON.parse(content) ... } catch { return { botName: "pi", accounts: {} }; }

referenceFindings.impact: Users may lose access to configured chat accounts/channels after a malformed write or manual edit and receive misleading 'no channels configured' behavior instead of a repairable parse error.
referenceFindings.recommendedFix: Distinguish ENOENT from JSON parse errors; surface parse errors in /chat-config, keep a .bak of the last valid config, and avoid overwriting corrupt config without confirmation.

referenceFindings.title: Conversation lock release can delete another session's lock
referenceFindings.claim: releaseConversationLock unconditionally unlinks the lock path without checking the owner id, so a stale runtime object or overlapping connect/disconnect path can remove a lock now owned by another process/session.

evidence.quote: export async function releaseConversationLock(conversation: ResolvedConversation): Promise<void> { await unlink(conversation.lockPath).catch(() => undefined); }

referenceFindings.impact: Concurrent workers or reconnect paths can lose mutual exclusion, leading to duplicate live connections and interleaved channel.jsonl writes.
referenceFindings.recommendedFix: Pass owner id to releaseConversationLock and unlink only if the file still contains that owner; otherwise leave the lock intact and report a stale-release warning.

referenceFindings.title: Discord catch-up can repeatedly fetch and download a large backlog on reconnect
referenceFindings.claim: Discord catchUp paginates messages after the last checkpoint and messageToInput downloads attachments for every message before ingestion filters can complete; if the checkpoint is stale or absent, reconnect can process a large backlog and all its attachments.

evidence.quote: while (true) { const batch = await channel.messages.fetch(cursor ? { after: cursor, limit: 100 } : { limit: 25 }); ... allMessages.push(...sorted); ... }
for (const attachment of message.attachments.values()) { const response = await fetch(attachment.url); ... await storeDownloadedAttachment(...) }

referenceFindings.impact: A reconnect can be slow, expensive, or memory/disk intensive, and may delay live responsiveness after downtime.
referenceFindings.recommendedFix: Bound catch-up by max messages/age/bytes, defer attachment download until a message is accepted and queued, and expose skipped-backlog status to users.

referenceFindings.title: tmux worker/status identifiers can collide after sanitization and truncation
referenceFindings.claim: tmuxSafeName replaces many distinct conversation ids with the same sanitized prefix and truncates to 100 characters; the same name is used for tmux sessions and status paths, so long/similar ids can collide.
referenceFindings.impact: Two configured channels can share a worker session/status file, causing one to appear already running or overwrite the other's status.
referenceFindings.recommendedFix: Append a short hash of the original conversationId or use a reversible safe encoding instead of lossy sanitize+truncate.

referenceFindings.title: Package has no automated test script despite broad integration surface
referenceFindings.claim: package.json only defines check/format and no test script, even though pi-chat has complex config, lock, rendering, attachment, and service-adapter behavior that can be unit-tested without live credentials.
referenceFindings.impact: Regressions in path handling, config corruption, lock ownership, chunking, and command parsing are likely to be caught late by manual/live testing.
referenceFindings.recommendedFix: Add node --test coverage for config load/save errors, lock owner release, runtime command parsing, attachment sanitization/size handling, and render chunking.

noIssueExpectations.claim: Remote control commands are gated through parseControlCommand and isAllowedInput before execution.
Outgoing chat_attach staging uses O_NOFOLLOW, file stat, sanitized basename, UUID, and wx write to avoid common overwrite/symlink issues.

knownUncertainties.question: Exact Telegram reconnect/cursor semantics require live API behavior or mocks to validate fully.
knownUncertainties.whyNotResolvedFromCode: The adapter polls external Telegram APIs and depends on update offsets/checkpoints.

knownUncertainties.question: Streaming preview behavior needs service-level integration tests for edit/delete rate limits and markdown behavior.
knownUncertainties.whyNotResolvedFromCode: Static code inspection cannot confirm remote platform behavior.
